trajectory_summary: This is a warm inbound call from an existing solar owner who came from an Enphase referral and arrived already knowing what he wanted — expanded panels, microinverters, and a battery backup. The rep ran the standard verify/bill/schedule flow competently and booked a specific in-home appointment, but she never engaged with the orphaned-system protocol (ownership status of the existing Namaste system, why Namaste dropped the ZIP, whether the existing inverters are functional) and let the customer's explicit 'not a cost-payback' framing pass without adapting the pitch.
outcome_dispute: The v1 tag is unknown, but the observed outcome is a clean booked appointment with day, time, and location confirmed — this should not be scored as fragile or tentative; the risk here is about deal quality/handoff completeness (orphaned-flow gaps), not booking mechanics.

observed_outcome.quote: K. So Thursday the thirtieth at four?
observed_outcome.reasoning: A specific day (Thursday the 30th) and time (4:00) were confirmed, the location was clarified as in-home ('it will just be at the house'), and scheduling was framed around 'you and your wife,' with the wife identified earlier as co-titleholder.

primary_coaching_focus.why: This customer is explicitly an existing-solar-owner lead, which triggers the orphaned_flow protocol (ownership type, prior company, system size, functioning status). None of those hard-DQ-relevant questions were asked before the rep moved into standard verify and booking — this is a process gap that could surface a disqualifying condition at the appointment instead of on this call.
